title: Model Admission Gateway and Canonical Pin Creation for Open Weights
creator: Anika Desai
description:
Goal: Implement an end-to-end admission gateway that accepts community/open-source weights, performs deterministic conversion to our runtime format, validates functional correctness and safety gates, generates a canonical version (pin) recommendation, and publishes a baseline performance profile to the model catalog. This ticket covers orchestration glue, high-level validation policy, and integration points with the profiling harness.

Scope: automated intake hooks, artifact verification (checksum, signature heuristics), safetensors/gguf/pt -> internal format conversion, lightweight static vetting (forbidden ops, unsupported layers), unit smoke tests, functional logits/sampling regression tests, prescribed eval set runs for latency/memory/throughput, and writing a pin manifest plus catalog metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- New artifact accepted by gateway results in an immutable canonical pin file in artifact-store and a catalog entry with profile metrics (p50 latency, p95, throughput at configured batch sizes, peak GPU memory).
- Conversion step is deterministic and logs a conversion provenance record (converter version, flags, input checksum).
- Functional regression test (deterministic seed on trimmed input) passes within tolerance compared to a reference inference (where available) or a golden smoke suite seeded by research.
- Safety heuristics flag models with unsupported ops or obviously malformed vocabularies and emit a triage ticket.
- Dashboard shows the profiling snapshot and the recommended pin (including quantization suggestion) as a draft until review.

Non-goals: automatic full evaluation on all RLHF benchmarks, deep model auditing for alignment, or automatic rollout to hosted inference without manual review for high-risk models.

Key trade-offs and decisions we made so far:
- Deterministic conversion: prefer replicable safetensors/gguf path even if it blocks some legacy pt formats for initial MVP. This reduces flaky validation runs at the cost of extra conversion tooling.
- Profiling vs. cost: we run a small but representative eval set (5 prompts per category) rather than exhaustive benchmarking to reduce resource consumption; we mark models for expanded benchmarking on-demand.
- Quantization handling: we will accept pre-quantized artifacts but perform a lightweight emulation pass to validate outputs; heavy quantization tuning will be a follow-up feature.

Risks and mitigations:
- Malformed weight bundles can cause converter crashes: mitigation = sandboxed conversion container + time/memory limits + pre-scan.
- Silent functional regressions due to converter bugs: mitigation = deterministic smoke tests and checksum-linked provenance.

Operational notes:
- Conversion runs in ephemeral k8s job with dedicated GPU types (A100-80GB for large models) and falls back to CPU-only conversion for small models.
- Pins are labeled with converter-version, profile-timestamp, and recommended runtime config.

Success metrics:
- 90% of accepted artifacts reach a draft catalog profile within 2 hours of intake in normal queue conditions.
- <5% conversion failure rate for artifacts passing initial pre-scan.
- Observability: every intake must produce a structured trace id that surfaces in Console rollups.
